title: Jagananna Amma Vodi — ₹15,000/year to mothers of school-going children
manifesto_text: Financial assistance of ₹15,000 per annum to mothers/guardians below the poverty line to keep children enrolled in school from Class I to XII.
assessment: Implemented from 2019-20. ₹19,000 crore disbursed across five years, benefiting 43 lakh families annually. Amount was ₹15,000/year; scheme was continued throughout the tenure.

title: Jagananna Gorumudda — eggs and milk in school mid-day meals
manifesto_text: Provide nutritious mid-day meals including eggs (4 days a week) and milk to all government school students.
assessment: Implemented from 2019-20. Eggs served four days a week and milk on remaining days across government schools, benefiting ~45 lakh students.

title: Jagananna Vidya Deevena — full fee reimbursement for higher education
manifesto_text: Complete fee reimbursement for SC/ST/BC/EBC/minority students pursuing degree, engineering, medical, and other higher education courses.
assessment: Implemented from 2019-20. Fees paid directly to colleges for eligible students pursuing ITI, polytechnic, degree, engineering, and medical programmes. Over ₹7,000 crore disbursed in 5 years.

title: Jagananna Vasati Deevena — hostel and food allowance for higher education students
manifesto_text: ₹10,000–₹20,000 per annum towards food and hostel expenses for students from ITI to postgraduate level.
assessment: Implemented from 2019-20. ₹10,000/year for ITI students, ₹15,000 for polytechnic, ₹20,000 for degree/PG. Amount credited directly to students' accounts. Total ~₹4,000 crore disbursed.

title: Convert government schools to English medium from Class I
manifesto_text: Introduce English as medium of instruction in all government schools starting from Class I to improve employability of students from economically weaker sections.
assessment: Implemented from 2020-21. All government schools switched to English medium from Class I. Policy was reversed by the NDA government after 2024.

title: Mana Badi Nadu Nedu — government school infrastructure overhaul
manifesto_text: Revamp government school infrastructure with clean toilets, drinking water, furniture, classrooms, and compound walls in a phased manner.
assessment: Implemented in multiple phases from 2020. Phases 1–3 covered ~64,000 schools, adding toilets, furniture, electricity, and classrooms. ₹10,000 crore+ invested across three phases.

title: YSR Rythu Bharosa — ₹13,500/year investment support to farmers
manifesto_text: Provide ₹12,500 per year investment support to farmer families owning land and ₹7,500 to tenant farmers, in addition to the PM-KISAN ₹6,000 central contribution.
assessment: Implemented from 2019-20. State government credited ₹7,500 to land-owning farmers (combined with PM-KISAN to total ₹13,500). Tenant farmers were also covered under YSR Rythu Bharosa-PM KISAN scheme. Total outlay ~₹2,000+ crore/year.

title: YSR Sunna Vaddi (Zero Interest Loans) — interest-free loans for women SHGs
manifesto_text: Waive interest on all outstanding SHG loans and provide zero-interest crop and livelihood loans to women self-help groups.
assessment: Implemented. SHG loan waivers worth ₹11,400 crore for ~2.7 lakh SHGs in 2019. Continued as YSR Sunna Vaddi, providing zero-interest loans up to ₹1 lakh per SHG member.

title: YSR Pension Kanuka — increase social security pensions to ₹3,000/month
manifesto_text: Increase old-age, widow, and disability pensions to ₹3,000 per month, and reduce the eligibility age for old-age pension from 65 to 60 years.
assessment: Implemented progressively. Pension started at ₹2,750/month in 2019 and was raised to ₹3,000 by 2022. Kidney patients received ₹10,000/month, severe disability ₹15,000/month. Age criterion lowered to 60 years as promised.

title: YSR Aarogyasri — expand health insurance to ₹25 lakh coverage for all families
manifesto_text: Expand health coverage under Aarogyasri to ₹25 lakh per family per year, include all treatments and procedures, and extend to families with annual income up to ₹5 lakh.
assessment: Implemented. YSR Aarogyasri expanded to ₹25 lakh coverage, encompassing over 1,000 additional procedures. Health cards (YSR Health Cards) issued to all eligible families.

title: Village Health Clinics — one primary health clinic per revenue village
manifesto_text: Establish a health and wellness centre (village clinic) in every revenue village to provide primary care without patients needing to travel to towns.
assessment: Implemented. YSR Village Clinics launched across AP; ~11,000+ clinics operational. Integrated with the village secretariat system for doorstep health services.

title: YSR Cheyutha — ₹75,000 over 4 years for BC/SC/ST/minority women aged 45–60
manifesto_text: Provide ₹75,000 in four annual instalments of ₹18,750 to SC/ST/BC/minority women aged 45–60 years for self-employment and livelihood support.
assessment: Implemented from 2020. Payments made to ~23 lakh women across the four-year cycle. Total expenditure ~₹17,000 crore.

title: YSR Kapu Nestham — ₹15,000/year financial assistance for Kapu community women
manifesto_text: Provide ₹15,000 per annum to women from the Kapu community for self-employment and livelihood support.
assessment: Implemented. ₹15,000/year credited to eligible Kapu women. Payments made annually across the tenure.

title: EBC Nestham — ₹15,000/year for economically backward class women
manifesto_text: Provide ₹15,000 per annum to women belonging to Economically Backward Classes (EBC / forward community poor) for livelihood support.
assessment: Implemented. Annual payments made to eligible EBC women throughout the tenure.

title: Jagananna Chedodu — financial aid to BC traditional profession workers
manifesto_text: Provide ₹10,000 per year to workers in traditional BC professions — barbers, washermen, tailors, weavers, goldsmiths, fishermen — to invest in their tools and trade.
assessment: Implemented. ₹10,000/year credited to beneficiaries from barber, washerman, tailor, weaver, goldsmith, and fishing communities. Payments made across the tenure.

title: Village/Ward Secretariat System — one volunteer per 50 households
manifesto_text: Establish village and ward secretariats across AP with one volunteer appointed for every 50 households at ₹5,000/month honorarium to deliver welfare schemes at the doorstep.
assessment: Implemented. ~2.5 lakh village and ward volunteers appointed across 15,000+ village secretariats. Volunteers facilitated delivery of pensions, Amma Vodi, Rythu Bharosa, and other DBT schemes. This is one of the largest last-mile governance initiatives in AP history.

title: Disha Act — fast-track courts and enhanced penalties for crimes against women
manifesto_text: Enact a special law to ensure speedy trial (within 21 days) and death penalty for rape and gang rape cases. Establish dedicated Disha police stations and fast-track courts across AP.
assessment: Implemented. AP Disha Act passed in December 2019, creating Disha police stations (one per district) and fast-track courts with 21-day trial mandate. First major legislation of the Jagan government.

title: Farmer Accident Insurance — ₹7 lakh for families of farmers who died by accident or suicide
manifesto_text: Pay ₹7 lakh compensation to the family of any farmer who dies in an accident or by suicide, funded through a state insurance scheme.
assessment: Implemented as YSR Farmers Group Insurance Scheme. ₹5 lakh accident insurance + ₹7 lakh suicide compensation policy. Payments made to affected families during the tenure.

title: 9 hours free daytime electricity for agriculture
manifesto_text: Provide 9 hours of free daytime power supply to agricultural pump-sets so that farmers can irrigate during the day using solar energy.
assessment: Implemented. Solar feeders and dedicated agricultural feeders ensured daytime power supply for farming. AP became one of the first states to operationalise daytime agricultural power at scale.

title: Interest-free crop loans for farmers
manifesto_text: Provide crop loans to all farmers at zero interest, with the state government bearing the interest burden on behalf of farmers.
assessment: Implemented. Interest subvention scheme continued, effectively making crop loans interest-free for farmers who repay on time. YSR Rythu Bharosa Kendras (RBKs) set up in ~10,778 locations for input delivery.

title: Land Titling Act — regularise assigned land for SC/ST/BC beneficiaries
manifesto_text: Enact legislation to regularise and provide clear land titles for all assigned lands given to SC/ST and BC communities, protecting them from illegal occupation.
assessment: Implemented as AP Land Titling Act (NRSS Act) in 2023. Provided legal titles to ~1.6 lakh acres of assigned land held by vulnerable communities. NDA government repealed this law after 2024 elections.

title: Register all housing scheme properties in women's names
manifesto_text: All government housing scheme houses and plots will be registered in the name of the woman of the household, empowering women with property rights.
assessment: Implemented as a standing policy. All YSR Housing Scheme units were registered in women's names as a rule from 2019.

title: YSR Housing Scheme — 25 lakh pucca houses in 5 years
manifesto_text: Construct 25 lakh pucca houses for the poor and homeless over a period of five years, with house pattas (deeds) in the name of the woman of the household.
assessment: Partially implemented. Around 15–18 lakh units completed or under construction by May 2024; target of 25 lakh not fully met within tenure. Significant construction achieved, though delayed by COVID-19 and material cost escalation.

title: Fill 2.3 lakh government job vacancies
manifesto_text: Fill all 2.3 lakh vacant government posts across departments through transparent recruitment within a fixed time schedule (Mega DSC and departmental calendar).
assessment: Partially implemented. Government claimed ~1.3 lakh appointments during 2019-2024; opposition disputed quality and completeness. Mega DSC and teacher recruitment happened but the full 2.3 lakh target was contested as not fully met.

title: AgriGold scam victims relief — ₹1,150 crore fund
manifesto_text: Create a ₹1,150 crore fund to compensate the ~13 lakh depositors who lost money in the AgriGold chit fund scam.
assessment: Partially implemented. Government set up an AgriGold Relief Fund and made partial payments through asset liquidation and state contributions. Full compensation to all 13 lakh victims was not achieved within the tenure.

title: Complete Polavaram irrigation project
manifesto_text: Complete the Polavaram multipurpose irrigation project to irrigate 7.2 lakh acres and provide drinking water to the Krishna-Godavari delta districts.
assessment: Ongoing. Polavaram construction progressed during 2019-2024 with spillway gates erected and civil works advanced, but the project was not commissioned by end of tenure. Completion remained elusive due to technical and Centre-state funding disputes.

title: Phased prohibition of alcohol
manifesto_text: Implement prohibition in three phases, ultimately banning liquor from all retail sale. Allow only premium establishments to serve alcohol.
assessment: Not fulfilled. The government introduced phased steps (reducing IMEFL outlets) but reversed course after revenue losses, ultimately expanding liquor availability. Full or even substantial prohibition was never implemented during the tenure.

title: Decentralised Three-Capital plan (Vizag executive, Amaravati legislative, Kurnool judicial)
manifesto_text: Decentralise governance by designating Visakhapatnam as the executive capital, Amaravati as the legislative capital, and Kurnool as the judicial capital for Andhra Pradesh.
assessment: Proposed but not implemented. Bills passed in AP Assembly but stayed by High Court. The three-capitals framework remained stalled in courts throughout the tenure. YSRCP abandoned the plan in practice and it was formally reversed by the NDA government after 2024.

title: ₹75,000 crore BC Welfare Fund over 5 years
manifesto_text: Allocate ₹75,000 crore over five years exclusively for welfare of Backward Classes through dedicated corporations, credit, and subsidy schemes.
assessment: Partially implemented. BC-specific allocations were made in budgets and through schemes like Jagananna Chedodu, Cheyutha, and BC Corporations, but a standalone fund of ₹75,000 crore was never formally constituted.

title: Restore SC/ST Sub-Plan funds and fill backlog posts
manifesto_text: Restore the mandatory SC/ST sub-plan allocation as per population proportion, release all held-back backlog posts, and ensure full utilisation of sub-plan funds.
assessment: Implemented. SC/ST Sub-plan allocations were restored to proportional levels (17% SCs, 7% STs) in budgets from 2019-20. Backlog posts in government departments were released for recruitment.

title: ₹3,000 crore agriculture price stabilisation fund
manifesto_text: Create a ₹3,000 crore price stabilisation fund to ensure farmers receive minimum support prices for their produce and prevent distress sales.
assessment: Partially implemented. YSR government set up the AP State Agricultural Mission for price support, and some crops received MSP procurement, but a dedicated standalone ₹3,000 crore fund was not formally constituted.

title: YSR Rythu Bharosa Kendras — one agri-service centre per village cluster
manifesto_text: Establish Rythu Bharosa Kendras at the village cluster level to provide seeds, fertilisers, pesticides, and market linkage to farmers without middlemen.
assessment: Implemented. ~10,778 RBKs operational across AP, one per 2-3 revenue villages. Managed by Village Agricultural Assistants (VAAs) and providing inputs, soil testing, crop advisory, and market information directly to farmers.

title: Jagananna Vidya Kanuka — free school kit (uniform, shoes, bag, books) every year
manifesto_text: Provide every government school student with a school kit — two sets of uniforms, a pair of shoes, socks, school bag, and textbooks — at the start of each academic year.
assessment: Implemented from 2020. Annual school kits distributed at the beginning of each academic year across government schools, benefiting ~42 lakh students per year.

title: Jagananna Thodu — digital tablets for higher-secondary and college students
manifesto_text: Provide digital tablets to students in Classes IX–XII and higher education to bridge the digital divide and support online learning.
assessment: Implemented. Tabs distributed to students from Class IX onwards under Jagananna Thodu. COVID-19 accelerated the rollout in 2020-21. Over 19 lakh students received tablets.

title: 50% reservation for women in local body elections
manifesto_text: Implement 50% reservation for women in all local body (panchayat, municipality) elected seats.
assessment: Implemented. AP government enacted 50% reservation for women in Panchayati Raj and urban local body elections, effective from 2021 local body polls.

title: Crop Cultivation Rights Cards for tenant farmers
manifesto_text: Issue Crop Cultivation Rights (CCR) cards to all tenant farmers so they can access formal credit, insurance, and government support schemes.
assessment: Implemented. CCR cards issued to ~21 lakh tenant farmers under the Andhra Pradesh Crop Cultivator Rights Act, enabling them to access bank loans, insurance, and Rythu Bharosa.

title: Rooftop solar power for residential consumers
manifesto_text: Provide rooftop solar installations to residential and small commercial consumers to reduce electricity bills and promote renewable energy.
assessment: Partially implemented. APSPDCL/APEPDCL ran solar rooftop programmes but scale was limited by grid absorption capacity. Target households not fully covered during the tenure.

title: Free sand policy — no cost sand for housing construction
manifesto_text: Provide sand free of cost for house construction, ending illegal sand mining and reducing the burden on home builders.
assessment: Implemented as the AP Sand Mining Policy 2020. Sand provided free at source (only transport charges applicable). Reduced cost of construction for housing beneficiaries, though enforcement of the free-at-source model had challenges.

title: 33% BC reservation in state legislature and local bodies
manifesto_text: Pass a resolution in the AP Assembly and lobby Parliament to enact a constitutional amendment for 33% reservation for Backward Classes in legislatures and local bodies.
assessment: Not achieved. A resolution was passed in the AP Assembly in 2021 demanding BC reservation in local bodies. However, the constitutional amendment from Centre was not forthcoming and local body elections with BC quota were stayed by the Supreme Court.
